one_line: AI-assisted crop diagnosis and constrained recovery planning for farmers.
what_it_does: Combines crop-photo analysis, weather, treatments, costs, and budget-constrained recovery plans through an agent-facing workflow.
leverage_rationale: The proposed structured tools could coordinate multiple agricultural decisions and preserve constraints more reliably than UI driving, but the packet provides no screenshots or video and only a truncated narrative.
leverage_evidence: Story describes analyze crop, check weather, find treatments, calculate costs, and build a recovery plan through WebMCP tools.
No frame sheets or operational evidence submitted.
execution_rationale: The story is coherent but execution is thinly evidenced: only a pitch and truncated written description are available.
execution_evidence: Demo is reported alive, but no visual or transcript evidence is included.
No public repository and no gallery images.
impact_rationale: Smallholder farmers have a concrete, consequential need for understandable crop diagnosis and affordable interventions; the stated budget-constrained workflow fits that need.
impact_evidence: Story identifies crop problems, weather, treatments, and cost as a farmer decision burden.
Example explicitly constrains recovery plan to a per-acre budget.
creativity_rationale: The farmer-goal/agent-complexity/farmer-approval model is a fresh synthesis for agricultural decision support, though the underlying capabilities are familiar.
creativity_evidence: Agent iteratively optimizes a recovery plan as the farmer changes budget constraints.
Human approval is retained as part of the stated interaction model.
usability_note: Plain-language farmer request is promising, but no interface evidence is supplied.
red_flags: No submitted images or video despite claims of an alive demo.
Execution and eligibility cannot be firmly established from the packet.
standouts: Concrete budget-constrained agricultural planning use case.
advance_reason: Promising concept and impact, but the packet lacks enough execution/WebMCP evidence for advancement.

one_line: Side-by-side apartment comparison workspace with exportable decision sheets.
what_it_does: Lets apartment hunters compare rents, fees, amenities, terms, and custom fields across listings, then export CSV or PDF.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools could make adding and normalizing listings more reliable than repetitive UI entry, but the described comparison outcome remains achievable with ordinary browser automation and the packet does not show agent interaction.
leverage_evidence: Story describes add_apartment, update_apartment_field, add_row, and export tools.
Use case is a structured comparison table with shared state, but no video or transcript demonstrates the agent surface.
execution_rationale: The written scope is coherent and gallery imagery is reported, but there is no frame/video evidence of the central workflow.
execution_evidence: Four gallery images and an alive demo are reported.
Description specifies editable fields, automatic best-value highlighting, and CSV/PDF export.
impact_rationale: Apartment hunters face a real, repeated comparison burden involving inconsistent fees and amenities; the product directly reduces that burden.
impact_evidence: Founder narrative describes manually retyping listings from multiple sources.
Core sheet compares rent, lease terms, fees, amenities, and notes.
creativity_rationale: A focused spreadsheet-style apartment comparison product is a competent take with a useful agent-enabled angle, but the category and interaction are familiar.
creativity_evidence: Custom comparison rows and automatic row-level best-value highlighting.
Agent-ready editing and export workflow.
usability_note: The side-by-side spreadsheet metaphor is clear and practical; actual usability is not visually verified here.
red_flags: No video or agent-invocation evidence in the packet.
Gallery/demo claims are not independently inspectable from the supplied evidence.
advance_reason: Impact is credible, but WebMCP differentiation and end-to-end execution are not demonstrated sufficiently.

one_line: Live chess coach that analyzes positions and teaches with board-native annotations.
what_it_does: Reads live board state, evaluates positions with local Stockfish, and uses highlights, arrows, candidate lines, and coaching messages to teach.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives the agent precise structured access to the live position and lets it teach in the same board state; a general UI-driving agent would be less reliable for FEN/legal-state reasoning and annotations.
leverage_evidence: Tools include get_board_state, evaluate_position, move history, highlights, arrows, candidate lines, and coach messages.
Frame sheets show a chess app with changing mid-game state and analysis panels.
execution_rationale: The product surfaces and tool loop are coherent and the frames show a functioning chess interface, though the contact sheets do not clearly demonstrate a full coaching interaction end to end.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show the chessboard, controls, and evolving analysis/history states.
Written scope explains local Stockfish evaluation and board annotations.
impact_rationale: Beginner and intermediate players have a clear learning need, and teaching the idea behind a move is valuable beyond merely returning engine lines.
impact_evidence: Description targets Elo-aware guidance and beginner/intermediate understanding.
Coaching requests include hints, threats, bad-move explanations, and candidate lines.
creativity_rationale: The interaction model turns an engine into a visual coach that preserves uncertainty and teaches directly on the board, a notably fresh synthesis.
creativity_evidence: Hint-without-answer and visual explanation modes.
Agent annotations are separated from the real game and can be cleared.
usability_note: Board-native annotations and player-level setting are promising; evidence does not fully show the complete user journey.
red_flags: Contact sheets are low-resolution and largely static; exact tool invocation is not legible.
standouts: Clear educational interaction model rather than answer-only engine output.
advance_reason: Strong leverage, credible execution evidence, and meaningful educational impact make this a clear advance.

one_line: Infinite whiteboard where agents inspect, create, connect, and style structured diagrams.
what_it_does: Turns a visual canvas into an agent-readable spatial workspace with diagram synthesis, state inspection, routing, templates, and themes.
leverage_rationale: The product’s core premise is structured spatial state shared between human and agent; precise object IDs, routing, layout, and canvas introspection are substantially impractical through generic pixel automation.
leverage_evidence: Story lists get_canvas_state, connect_elements, create_diagram, apply_theme, and 11 registered tools.
Screenshot visibly shows an architecture diagram on an infinite whiteboard; frame evidence includes node/graph workflow states.
execution_rationale: The broad tool suite, visible diagram output, and multiple frame sheets establish a coherent, ambitious product with an apparently functioning canvas, though frame readability is limited.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot shows a populated AI inference architecture diagram with connected nodes.
Written evidence describes auto-layout, collision avoidance, telemetry, and bidirectional co-creation.
Public repository, tests, and MIT license are claimed.
impact_rationale: Architects, developers, and collaborative thinkers have a real need for spatial modeling; making diagrams agent-addressable can reduce tedious layout and editing work.
impact_evidence: Use cases include backend architecture, data pipelines, and brainstorming.
Agent can synthesize, inspect, route, and restyle diagrams while humans work on the canvas.
creativity_rationale: An agent-native spatial canvas is a memorable interaction model, and the submission pursues the idea deeply through typed spatial operations and human-agent co-creation.
creativity_evidence: Agent detects human-drawn elements and routes connectors from stable canvas state.
Combines visual whiteboard interaction with structured agent operations and live telemetry.
usability_note: Visible canvas and controls are understandable, but dense feature breadth may require refinement.
red_flags: Frame sheets are dark and low-resolution, so exact interactions are only partly inspectable.
standouts: WebMCP is central rather than decorative.
Strong spatial shared-state concept with concrete tool semantics.
advance_reason: Transformative leverage and unusually original spatial interaction, backed by visible product evidence.

one_line: Cited theatre research workspace shared by humans and browser agents.
what_it_does: Searches theatre sources, answers questions, compares productions, and presents page-level passages and citations in a shared workspace.
leverage_rationale: Typed search and comparison tools returning page-level evidence are materially more reliable and auditable than an agent manually navigating scattered theatre pages and PDFs.
leverage_evidence: Three tools are specified: ask_theatre, search_theatre_archive, and compare_productions.
Frame sheets show a research/discovery interface progressing to knowledge and evidence views.
execution_rationale: The screenshot and frame sheets show a coherent research product and evolving result/evidence screens, though the exact agent tool call is not legible.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot shows research-oriented interface and tool/output panel.
Frames show discovery input, knowledge/results panel, expanded evidence text, and cited-answer presentation.
Public repository and alive demo are reported.
impact_rationale: Theatre researchers, students, and enthusiasts face fragmented sources; source-grounded answers and production comparison offer credible niche value.
impact_evidence: Story identifies scattered articles, PDFs, venue announcements, and historical lists.
Outputs include supporting excerpts and page numbers.
creativity_rationale: A focused, evidence-first theatre research agent is a fresh domain-specific synthesis, though the underlying research-assistant pattern is known.
creativity_evidence: Shared visible workspace keeps human and agent on the same evidence.
Compare-productions supports user-selected focus such as venue, opening date, and run length.
usability_note: The discovery-to-evidence flow appears understandable, with citations visible in the intended output.
red_flags: Low-resolution frames do not verify exact WebMCP calls or citation correctness.
advance_reason: Meaningful WebMCP leverage and credible product/evidence flow for a well-defined research audience.

one_line: Policy-bounded delegate agent that handles routine communications and escalates exceptions.
what_it_does: Lets a person brief a stand-in agent, set live boundaries, route approvals and escalations, and preserve trusted human handoff during absence.
leverage_rationale: The claimed product depends on live, identity- and state-dependent tool surfaces enforcing delegation boundaries; generic UI automation cannot comparably guarantee the same policy-aware handoff.
leverage_evidence: Story says the WebMCP surface changes based on who is looking and current state, computed live in the browser.
Frames show Maya’s Relay recipients/test interface, but exact agent action is not legible.
execution_rationale: The concept and policy model are coherent and the frames show a real Relay interface, but the contact sheets mostly show a static recipients screen rather than a full delegated conversation and escalation loop.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show Maya’s Relay recipients/test UI.
Narrative specifies briefing, policy boundaries, approvals, and escalation behavior.
Public repository and alive demo are reported.
impact_rationale: People facing medical procedures, emergencies, custody handoffs, or work interruptions have a real need for bounded continuity without granting unrestricted access.
impact_evidence: Story gives concrete planned and unplanned absence scenarios.
Product preserves trusted-person escalation for actions outside the boundary.
creativity_rationale: Delegating judgment rather than credentials, with a dynamically enforced boundary and explicit human fallback, is a memorable and ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Distinguishes access from judgment and routes out-of-policy work to a trusted person.
Identity/state-dependent browser tool surface is part of the product model.
usability_note: The safety model is compelling, but the visible evidence does not demonstrate the full setup-to-handoff flow.
red_flags: Frames show mostly static recipient-management UI; core policy enforcement and escalation are not visibly demonstrated.
High-stakes use cases require especially strong verification in later review.
standouts: Concrete human fallback rather than unrestricted autonomy.
advance_reason: Exceptional concept and impact with strong claimed WebMCP indispensability; advance despite incomplete visual proof.

one_line: Human-gated 3D studio where agents inspect and stage exact reversible scene edits.
what_it_does: Exposes structured scene inspection, object search, focus, and revision-checked preview tools while reserving Apply for a human artist.
leverage_rationale: Stable object identity, canonical revisions, exact staged transactions, and human-only commit create a collaboration model that generic UI-driving cannot reproduce reliably or safely.
leverage_evidence: Transcript demonstrates inspect, find, focus, and stage calls against the real scene and revision.
Demo stages rename/material edits, shows before/after preview, then requires one visible human Apply.
Frames show 3D studio, scene hierarchy/inspector, preview, and activity states.
execution_rationale: The 174-second narrated demo gives unusually complete end-to-end evidence: inspect, resolve object, focus, stage, review, human apply, revision advance, and activity history.
execution_evidence: Transcript covers the complete workflow and explicitly reports canonical revision behavior.
Frame sheets show the 3D scene/studio and staged preview states.
Public repository, tests, and alive demo are reported.
impact_rationale: 3D artists need precise scene edits without surrendering authorship; reversible previews and revision-safe approval directly address that professional workflow need.
impact_evidence: Product targets dense, stateful 3D editing with many objects and materials.
Human Apply, exact diff, stale rejection, and audit history support artist control.
creativity_rationale: The deliberate absence of a commit tool and the staged human-gated transaction are an original, deeply pursued interaction model for agent-assisted creative work.
creativity_evidence: Agent prepares reversible edits; human remains sole canonical approver.
Proposal authorship and human approval are distinguished in activity history.
usability_note: The staged diff and visible Apply boundary make the workflow legible and controllable for artists.
standouts: Best end-to-end evidence in the packet.
WebMCP is the collaboration and safety model, not a CRUD wrapper.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage and execution with complete narrated proof of the central workflow.
